method.note: This pass replaces an earlier recall-only pass. WebSearch worked (about 100 queries, each returning encyclopedias, library and publisher records, university pages and the Nobel and Pulitzer sites). WebFetch could not resolve any host and curl through the proxy returned 403, so no primary text was read; every check rests on WebSearch result summaries, and where a summary did not mention a claim it is listed under remainingDoubts and not counted as search-confirmed. claimsChecked counts discrete dated, attributed, "first", numeric, named-person and term claims examined; checkedWithSearch is the part confirmed or corrected against a search result this pass; the rest are standard facts (period boundaries, form definitions) held from solid knowledge and consistent with the library. The edits made by the earlier recall-only pass were all re-examined with search and held (priorPassChangesRechecked).

discrepanciesBetweenSources: Waley's Genji: one catalogue gave 1921 to 1933 and another 1926 to 1933; Britannica and the volume-by-volume records give 1925 to 1933. Kept 1925 to 1933.
Saikaku, The Life of an Amorous Man: one reference gave 1683; the Waseda University Library record gives October 1682. Kept 1682.
Kokinshu: sources say ordered about 905, last poem possibly 914, finished form about 920. Text now says ordered in about 905.
Wang Wen-hsing, Family Catastrophe: serialised 1972 to 1973, book edition 1973. Text keeps 1973.
Mo Yan, Red Sorghum: novella in People's Literature, 1986; five parts joined as a novel in 1987 (the Nobel biography dates the novel 1987). Text and works field keep 1986, the first publication.
Lao She, Camel Xiangzi: serial September 1936 to May 1937 in one record, January 1937 start in another. Text says serialised 1936 to 1937; works field keeps the library year 1937.
Ba Jin, Family: serialised 1931 to 1932, book 1933. Text says serialised from 1931.
Jupiter Hammon: broadside dated 1761 by most sources, 1760 by one. Text keeps 1761.
Dery on Afrofuturism: 1993 in most sources, 1994 in some (the essay was reprinted in a 1994 book). Text now says early 1990s.
Ntozake Shange, for colored girls: 1974 to 1976 depending on source. The text gives no year.
Nihon shoki end point and Man'yoshu compilation details vary by source; the text makes no claim on either.

softened.was: a four-part scheme ... borrowed from the pattern of Chinese verse, is often cited

The bullet already says how far it describes Japanese fiction is debated, and it was kept.
